title: Tom Kha Gai
subtitle: Thai coconut and galangal chicken soup
excerpt: A fragrant, silky Thai soup of chicken in coconut milk scented with galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and lemongrass. Balanced between sour, salty, and gently hot, it is one of the most elegant soups in Thai cooking.
sourceNotes: Tom kha gai translates as galangal chicken soup and is a central dish in both Thai and Lao cooking. The defining ingredient is galangal, a relative of ginger with a sharper, more piney flavour. This recipe uses fresh ginger as a substitute, which is more widely available and produces a slightly different but equally good result.

content.text: This soup uses fresh ginger as a substitute for galangal, which is the traditional ingredient. Galangal has a more resinous, woody flavour than ginger and is available in Asian grocery stores; use it in the same quantity if you can find it. Lemongrass is another aromatic that defines the soup; if it is available to you, bash one stalk and add it with the kaffir lime leaves, removing before serving. Do not let the soup boil hard once the coconut milk is in; a hard boil can make the coconut milk split.

items.prepNote: peeled and sliced into coins (or galangal if available)

content.text: Put the stock, ginger coins, and kaffir lime leaves into the saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer over a medium heat and cook for 10 minutes to infuse the aromatics.
Pour in the coconut milk and add the palm sugar. Stir to combine and return to a gentle simmer.
Add the mushrooms and sliced chicken. Simmer gently for 6 to 8 minutes until the chicken is cooked through. Do not let the soup boil.
Add the fish sauce and most of the lime juice. Taste and adjust the balance: add more fish sauce for saltiness, lime for sourness, palm sugar for sweetness.
Ladle into bowls. Scatter over the sliced chilli and fresh coriander. Serve with steamed jasmine rice.

items.symptom: Coconut milk has split into oil and watery liquid.
items.cause: The soup was allowed to boil hard after the coconut milk was added.
items.fix: Keep the soup at a gentle simmer; never allow it to boil.

items.symptom: Soup tastes flat despite all the aromatics.
items.cause: Not enough lime juice or fish sauce was added at the end.
items.fix: Season boldly with lime and fish sauce; taste and adjust.

items.cause: Breast meat overcooked in the hot broth.
items.fix: Simmer just until the pink is gone; 6 minutes is usually enough.
